sections.title: Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: Revenue growth includes two acquisition step-ups (Altran FY2020, WNS Q4-FY2025) that are not organic; organic/constant-currency growth was flat-to-negative for six consecutive quarters through Q3-2025.

charts.title: Statutory Operating Margin
charts.annotation: This is the STATUTORY margin (operating income / revenue), not Capgemini's guided “operating margin” APM. The APM excludes restructuring (Fit-for-Growth, ~€700m cumulative FY2026-27), M&A amortization, SBC and pension items. H1 FY2026: statutory 7.3% vs APM 12.5% — a 5.2pp gap. FY2026 APM guidance is 13.6-13.8%.

sections.title: Cash Generation & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: Three different free-cash-flow numbers get reported for Capgemini every year — they are not interchangeable, see the FCF chart help.

charts.title: Free Cash Flow (Statutory OCF − Capex)
charts.annotation: H1 FY2018 FreeCashFlow is −€2m — note the series crosses zero, so no log toggle is offered. H1 rows run structurally near zero every year; Capgemini's cash generation is heavily H2-weighted (working-capital unwind + year-end collections).

charts.title: Three FCF Definitions (FY2025)
charts.annotation: Single FY2025 snapshot from the DCF JSON. Statutory OCF−capex: €2,195m. Capgemini's own ‘organic free cash flow’ APM: €1,949m — this additionally deducts lease principal and net interest and is heavily H2-weighted (H1 FY2026 was only €37m; never annualize the H1 figure). DCF owner FCF: €1,633m = OCF − capex − lease principal (€296m) − SBC (€266m), the fully-costed distributable-cash basis the valuation runs on.

charts.title: Total Debt vs Cash
charts.annotation: Net debt (company-disclosed, ex-lease-liabilities basis, not simply TotalDebt − Cash) tripled in 18 months: €2,107m (Dec-2024) → €5,306m (Dec-2025) → €6,454m (Jun-2026) funding the ~$3.3bn WNS Holdings acquisition that closed 2025-10-17. Goodwill (~€14.7bn) now exceeds shareholders' equity (~€11.6bn).

charts.title: Stock-Based Compensation
charts.annotation: Grew from €32m (FY2015) to €266m (FY2025), roughly 1.2% of revenue — small by US tech standards but fully expensed in the DCF's owner-FCF base rather than added back.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Total group revenue across Strategy & Transformation, Applications & Technology, and Operations & Engineering.

For Capgemini: FY2025 revenue was €22,465m. The 5yr/10yr revenue CAGRs (7.2%/6.6%) are ACQUISITION-DRIVEN, not organic — Altran was consolidated in 2020 and WNS Holdings (~$3.3bn, plus Cloud4C) closed 2025-10-17 and is reflected from Q4 FY2025. Organic/constant-currency growth was flat-to-negative for six consecutive quarters (Q1-2024 through Q3-2025) before inflecting positive; ~5 points of the guided FY2026 +8.5-9.0% cc growth is WNS/Cloud4C scope, not organic delivery.

What to watch:

  • Book-to-bill ratio: 1.08x FY2025, 1.04x H1-2026 — the leading indicator for whether organic growth holds
  • Whether growth ex-WNS/Cloud4C scope turns negative again once the acquisition laps in FY2027
  • Applications & Technology (63% of revenue, the core people-based delivery business) is most exposed to AI-driven demand or deflation of billable-hour pricing

operatingMargin.title: Statutory Operating Margin
operatingMargin.content:
Operating income divided by revenue, as reported under IFRS — includes restructuring, M&A amortization, SBC and pension items.

For Capgemini: this is deliberately NOT the company's guided “operating margin” APM (Alternative Performance Measure), which strips out recurring restructuring costs (the Fit-for-Growth program, ~€700m cumulative over FY2026-27), M&A-related amortization, SBC and pension items. The gap is large and persistent: H1 FY2026 statutory margin was 7.3% against a 12.5% APM — a 5.2 percentage-point difference. FY2026 APM guidance is 13.6-13.8%, maintained despite the statutory drag. The DCF values this business on the STATUTORY basis on the view that recurring restructuring is a real recurring cost, not a one-off to be added back every year.

What to watch:

  • Whether Fit-for-Growth restructuring actually tapers after FY2027 (bull case) or proves to be a permanent cost of staying competitive (base/bear case)
  • Any quarter where the statutory margin misses even though the APM holds — the DCF's central risk flag

eps.title: EPS & Shares Outstanding
eps.content:
Statutory diluted earnings per share, plotted against the shares-outstanding count on the secondary axis.

For Capgemini: the share count has fallen from ~171m (FY2023) to 168.3m (H1 FY2026) on continuous buybacks (€543m repurchased in FY2025, €315m in H1 FY2026 alone) that roughly offset SBC-driven dilution. The DCF holds the share count FLAT at 168.3m going forward — charging further buyback-funded reduction on top of a fully-expensed SBC charge would double-count the capital return.

What to watch:

  • Whether buybacks continue at the same pace now that net debt has tripled to fund the WNS acquisition — capital allocation priorities may shift toward deleveraging

fcf.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow (Statutory)
fcf.content:
Statutory operating cash flow less capital expenditure, compared against net income.

For Capgemini: FY2025 free cash flow was €2,195m. This series is strongly seasonal within a fiscal year — H1 FY2018 FreeCashFlow was actually NEGATIVE (−€2m), and H1 rows generally run close to zero every year because Capgemini's cash generation is heavily H2-weighted (working-capital unwind and year-end client collections). Never annualize an H1 FCF figure by doubling it.

What to watch:

  • See the “Three FCF Definitions” chart for how this statutory figure differs from Capgemini's own ‘organic free cash flow’ APM and from the DCF's owner-FCF base — they are not interchangeable and differ by hundreds of millions of euros

ownerFcf.title: Three FCF Definitions (FY2025 Snapshot)
ownerFcf.content:
A single FY2025 comparison, sourced from the DCF JSON rather than the CSV time series, of three cash-flow measures that all get called ‘free cash flow’ for Capgemini.

For Capgemini: (1) Statutory OCF − capex: €2,195m — the naive number, but it omits ~€290m/yr of IFRS-16 lease principal repayments that are a real cash cost. (2) Capgemini's own ‘organic free cash flow’ APM: €1,949m — this additionally deducts lease principal AND net interest, and management guides FY2026 to ~€1.8-1.9bn on this basis; it is heavily H2-seasonal (H1 FY2026 was only €37m, never annualize it). (3) DCF owner FCF: €1,633m = OCF (€2,482m) − capex (€287m) − lease principal (€296m) − SBC (€266m) — the fully-costed, distributable-cash basis the valuation actually runs on, lower than both other figures because it also charges the full SBC expense.

What to watch:

  • The organic-FCF APM is post-interest, which double-counts against the separate net-debt bridge — that is why the DCF does not use it as its base, even though it is the number management guides on

netDebt.title: Total Debt vs Cash
netDebt.content:
Gross balance-sheet debt and cash & equivalents from the CSV. Company-disclosed net debt (which excludes lease liabilities, per Capgemini's own definition) is the figure actually used in the DCF's valuation bridge and does not equal TotalDebt − CashAndEquivalents exactly.

For Capgemini: company-disclosed net debt tripled in 18 months: €2,107m (Dec-2024) → €5,306m (Dec-2025) → €6,454m (Jun-2026), funding the ~$3.3bn acquisition of WNS Holdings that closed 2025-10-17 (plus Cloud4C). Goodwill (~€14.7bn) now EXCEEDS shareholders' equity (~€11.6bn) — a balance-sheet amplifier if the acquisition underperforms.

What to watch:

  • Pace of deleveraging back toward Capgemini's historical ~1x EBITDA leverage — the DCF's bull case requires visible progress here
  • Peak leverage coinciding with the AI-deflation risk to the core delivery model is the balance-sheet amplifier cited as the reason the bear scenario is weighted above the house default (30% vs 15%)

sbc.title: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.content:
Share-based payment expense as reported in the consolidated cash flow statement add-back.

For Capgemini: €266m in FY2025, roughly 1.2% of revenue — modest by global tech standards, but fully expensed (not added back) in the DCF's owner-FCF base. Continuous buybacks (€543m FY2025) roughly offset the dilution this creates, keeping the share count flat-to-falling.

What to watch:

  • Whether buyback pace slows now that net debt has tripled, which would let SBC-driven dilution show through in the share count for the first time in several years

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — statutory OCF less capex, IFRS-16 lease principal & full SBC charge
dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (~8%, includes WNS/Cloud4C scope)
dcf.current_price_note_2: Bear case weighted 30% (double the house default): Capgemini's own URD risk factors concede AI-driven deflation of the billable-hours pyramid model, and it coincides with peak leverage (net debt ~3x in 18 months) and goodwill exceeding equity. The model does not pick a side — base/bull read the 30% de-rating as overdone against raised guidance; the bear read is that the de-rating is the market correctly pricing a structural change to the delivery model.
